passages.text: As Jesus left the temple and was walking away, His disciples came up to Him to point out its buildings.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the temple.
He walked away.
His disciples came to Him.
They wanted to show Him the buildings of the temple.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπορεύετο καὶ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτῷ τὰς οἰκοδομὰς τοῦ ἱεροῦ

passages.text: “Do you see all these things?” He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He answered them.
He said, “Do you see all these things?”
He referred to the buildings of the temple.
He said, “Truly, I tell you this.”
“Not one stone here will remain on another.”
“Every stone will be thrown down.”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ βλέπετε ταῦτα πάντα ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται

passages.text: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives.
The disciples came to Jesus privately.
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Tell us when these things will happen.”
They also asked, “What will be the sign of your coming?”
They asked, “What will be the sign of the end of the age?”
passages.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν λέγοντες Εἰπὲ ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον τῆς σῆς παρουσίας καὶ συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος

passages.text: Jesus answered, “See to it that no one deceives you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He answered them.
He said, “Be careful.
Make sure no one deceives you.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ

passages.text: For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples on the Mount of Olives.
He warned them about the future.
Many people will come using My name.
They will say, “I am the Christ.”
These people will deceive many others.
passages.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ Χριστός καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν

passages.text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about the future.
You will hear about wars.
You will hear rumors about wars.
Do not be alarmed.
These things must happen.
The end will not come yet.
passages.original: μελλήσετε δὲ ἀκούειν πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων ὁρᾶτε μὴ θροεῖσθε δεῖ γὰρ γενέσθαι ἀλλ’ οὔπω ἐστὶν τὸ τέλος

passages.text: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the future.
He warned them about coming troubles.
One nation will attack another nation.
One kingdom will fight another kingdom.
Famines will happen in different places.
Earthquakes will also happen in different places.
passages.original: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπὶ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν καὶ ἔσονται λιμοὶ καὶ σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους

passages.text: All these are the beginning of birth pains.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the future.
He described wars, rumors of wars, famines, and earthquakes.
He said these events must happen.
He explained that these events are not the end.
He said all these things are only the beginning of birth pains.
passages.original: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων

passages.text: Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His followers.
He warned them about the future.
People will hand you over to be persecuted.
They will kill you.
All nations will hate you.
They will hate you because of My name.
passages.original: Τότε παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου

passages.text: At that time many will fall away and will betray and hate one another, and many false prophets will arise and mislead many.
passages.sermon:
At that time, many people will fall away from faith.
Many people will betray each other.
Many people will hate each other.
Many false prophets will appear.
Many false prophets will mislead many people.
passages.original: καὶ τότε σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀλλήλους παραδώσουσιν καὶ μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους καὶ πολλοὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐγερθήσονται καὶ πλανήσουσιν πολλούς

passages.text: Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.
passages.sermon: Wickedness will increase.\r\nMost people will stop loving others.\r\nTheir love will become cold.
passages.original: Καὶ διὰ τὸ πληθυνθῆναι τὴν ἀνομίαν ψυγήσεται ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν πολλῶν

passages.text: But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
passages.sermon: The person who perseveres to the end will be saved.\r\nPerseverance means continuing in faith and obedience.\r\nSalvation comes to those who endure until the end.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται

passages.text: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the end times.
He said the gospel of the kingdom will be preached.
People will preach this gospel in all the world.
The gospel will be a testimony to all nations.
After this, the end will come.
passages.original: Καὶ κηρυχθήσεται τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ εἰς μαρτύριον πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ τότε ἥξει τὸ τέλος

passages.text: So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination of desolation,’ described by the prophet Daniel (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about a future event.
He said, “You will see the abomination of desolation.”
The prophet Daniel described this abomination.
It will stand in the holy place.
Let the reader understand this warning.
When this happens, people in Judea must flee.
They must go to the mountains.
passages.original: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε Τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη

passages.text: Let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve anything from his house.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the end times.
He warned them about great danger coming.
He said, “If someone is on the housetop, that person must not come down.”
That person must not go inside to take anything from the house.
They must leave immediately.
passages.original: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι τὰ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.
passages.sermon:
Jesus warned his disciples about a coming time of great trouble.
\r\nHe spoke to people living in Judea.
\r\nHe said, “If you are in the field, do not go back.”
\r\nDo not return to get your cloak.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!
passages.sermon:
Jesus warned about a coming time of great trouble.
This trouble will be worse than anything before.
Pregnant women will suffer in those days.
Mothers who are nursing babies will also suffer.
Those days will be very hard for them.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις

passages.text: Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
\r\nHe warned them about a coming time of great trouble.
\r\nHe told them to pray.
\r\nHe said, "Pray that you will not have to flee in the winter."
\r\nHe also said, "Pray that you will not have to flee on the Sabbath."
passages.original: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος μηδὲ σαββάτῳ

passages.text: For at that time there will be great tribulation, unmatched from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the end times.
He warned them about a coming period of great suffering.
This suffering will be very severe.
No other trouble like it has happened since the world began.
Nothing like it has ever happened before.
Nothing like it will ever happen again.
passages.original: ἔσται γὰρ τότε θλῖψις μεγάλη οἵα οὐ γέγονεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κόσμου ἕως τοῦ νῦν οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ γένηται

passages.text: If those days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.
passages.sermon:
God will shorten those days.
If God did not shorten those days, no one would survive.
God will shorten those days for the sake of the elect.
The elect are God’s chosen people.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολοβώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ διὰ δὲ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι

passages.text: At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about the end times.
He warned them about a time of great trouble.
He said, "At that time, someone may say to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!'" 
Someone may also say, "There He is!"
Do not believe them.
passages.original: Τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ Χριστός ἤ Ὧδε μὴ πιστεύσητε

passages.text: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders that would deceive even the elect, if that were possible.
passages.sermon:
False Christs will appear.
False prophets will also appear.
They will perform great signs.
They will perform great wonders.
These signs and wonders will try to deceive people.
If it were possible, even the elect would be deceived.
passages.original: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα μεγάλα καὶ τέρατα ὥστε πλανῆσαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς

passages.text: See, I have told you in advance.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus warned them about future events.
Jesus said these things before they happened.
Jesus told them in advance.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν

passages.text: So if they tell you, ‘There He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or, ‘Here He is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus warned his disciples about false Christs and false prophets.
These deceivers will try to mislead people.
Some people may say, “Look, he is in the wilderness.”
Do not go out to the wilderness.
Others may say, “Look, he is in the inner rooms.”
Do not believe them.
passages.original: Ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν Ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστίν μὴ ἐξέλθητε Ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις μὴ πιστεύσητε

passages.text: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
The coming of Jesus will be clear to everyone.
Lightning comes from the east.
Lightning flashes and can be seen as far as the west.
In the same way, everyone will see the coming of Jesus.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.
passages.sermon: Vultures gather where there is a carcass.\r\nThey come together at the place of the dead body.
passages.original: ὅπου ἐὰν ᾖ τὸ πτῶμα ἐκεῖ συναχθήσονται οἱ ἀετοί

passages.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the end times.
He described what will happen after the great trouble of those days.
The sun will become dark.
The moon will not shine.
The stars will fall from the sky.
The powers in the heavens will be shaken.
passages.original: Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων Ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται Καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς Καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται

passages.text: At that time the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory.
passages.sermon:
The Son of Man is Jesus Christ.
At that time, a sign will appear in heaven.
This sign will show that Jesus is coming.
All the tribes of the earth will see this sign.
All the tribes of the earth will mourn.
They will see Jesus, the Son of Man.
He will come on the clouds of heaven.
He will come with power.
He will come with great glory.
passages.original: Καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ τότε κόψονται πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὄψονται τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς

passages.text: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus will send out His angels.
The angels will go with a loud trumpet call.
The angels will gather His chosen people.
They will gather them from every direction.
They will gather them from one end of the heavens to the other.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ μετὰ σάλπιγγος μεγάλης καὶ ἐπισυνάξουσιν τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρων οὐρανῶν ἕως τῶν ἄκρων αὐτῶν

passages.text: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to learn a lesson from the fig tree.
The fig tree has branches.
When the branches become tender, something happens.
The branches begin to sprout leaves.
When you see this, you know something important.
You know that summer is near.
passages.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς γένηται ἁπαλὸς καὶ τὰ φύλλα ἐκφύῃ γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος

passages.text: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He described signs that would happen before His coming.
He said, “You will see all these things.”
When you see these things, you will know something important.
You will know that He is near.
He is right at the door.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅταν ἴδητε πάντα ταῦτα γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις

passages.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Truly, I tell you this.”
This generation will not pass away.
All these things will happen before this generation passes away.
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα ταῦτα γένηται

passages.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
He says, "Heaven will pass away.
Earth will pass away.
My words will never pass away."
passages.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσεται οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρέλθωσιν

passages.text: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking about the day and hour of His coming.
No one knows the exact day or hour.
The angels in heaven do not know.
The Son does not know.
Only the Father knows.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν οὐδὲ ὁ Υἱός εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατὴρ μόνος

passages.text: As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking about His return.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
The coming of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.
In the days of Noah, people lived as usual before the flood.
In the same way, people will not expect the coming of the Son of Man.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ Νῶε οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.
passages.sermon:
Before the flood, people lived their daily lives.
They ate food.
They drank.
They got married.
They gave their children in marriage.
They continued these things until the day Noah entered the ark.
passages.original: ὡς γὰρ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ταῖς πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες γαμοῦντες καὶ γαμίζοντες ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν

passages.text: And they were oblivious, until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
passages.sermon:
The people did not understand what was coming.
They continued their lives without awareness.
Then the flood came.
The flood swept all the people away.
The coming of the Son of Man will be like this.
People will not expect it.
Sudden judgment will come.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ἕως ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἦρεν ἅπαντας οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἡ παρουσία τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.
passages.sermon: Two men will be in the field.\r\nOne man will be taken.\r\nOne man will be left.
passages.original: τότε ἔσονται δύο ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ εἷς παραλαμβάνεται καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται

passages.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and the other left.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about His return.
He called Himself the Son of Man.
He said people would not expect the time of His coming.
He gave examples to explain this.
Two women will be grinding at the mill.
One woman will be taken.
The other woman will be left.
passages.original: δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐν τῷ μύλῳ μία παραλαμβάνεται καὶ μία ἀφίεται

passages.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to his disciples.
He tells them to keep watch.
You do not know the day your Lord will come.
Stay alert.
Be ready for your Lord’s coming.
passages.original: Γρηγορεῖτε οὖν ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται

passages.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.
passages.sermon:
A homeowner owns a house.
A thief plans to break into the house at night.
The homeowner does not know when the thief will come.
If the homeowner had known the exact time the thief would come,
he would have stayed awake.
He would have watched carefully.
He would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
passages.original: ἐκεῖνο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ φυλακῇ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται ἐγρηγόρησεν ἂν καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴασεν διορυχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus will come again.
You do not know when Jesus will come.
You do not expect the hour when he comes.
Therefore, you must be ready.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι ὅτι ᾗ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὥρᾳ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται

passages.text: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time?
passages.sermon:
The master owns a household.
The master chooses one servant.
This servant is faithful.
This servant is wise.
The master puts this servant in charge of his household.
The master gives the servant a task.
The servant must give food to the other servants.
The servant must give the food at the proper time.
passages.original: Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς δοῦλος καὶ φρόνιμος ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκετείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν τροφὴν ἐν καιρῷ

passages.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
passages.sermon:
A servant can be faithful and wise.
A master puts this servant in charge of his household.
The servant gives food to others at the proper time.
The master returns unexpectedly.
The master finds the servant doing his duty.
That servant is blessed.
passages.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει οὕτως ποιοῦντα

passages.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
Jesus describes a faithful and wise servant.
The master finds this servant doing his duty.
Jesus says, “Truly, I tell you.”
The master will put this servant in charge of all his possessions.
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν

passages.text: But suppose that servant is wicked and says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’
passages.sermon: A servant can be wicked.\r\nA wicked servant thinks in his heart.\r\nHe says, “My master will be away a long time.”
passages.original: Ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ κακὸς δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Χρονίζει μου ὁ κύριος

passages.text: And he begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.
passages.sermon: The wicked servant begins to beat his fellow servants.\r\nHe eats with drunkards.\r\nHe drinks with drunkards.
passages.original: καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ ἐσθίῃ δὲ καὶ πίνῃ μετὰ τῶν μεθυόντων

passages.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.
passages.sermon:
The servant is wicked.
The master is away for a long time.
The master will return.
The servant does not expect the master to return on that day.
The servant does not know the hour the master will return.
The master will come on a day the servant does not expect.
The master will come at an hour the servant does not know.
passages.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει

passages.text: Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
passages.sermon:
The master will punish that servant.
He will cut him to pieces.
He will put him with the hypocrites.
In that place, people will weep.
In that place, people will gnash their teeth.
passages.original: καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων
